claims.statement: ITU's 2025 report separates network availability from meaningful use, identifying affordability, devices, skills, quality and safety as persistent barriers.
claims.boundary: Global aggregate and framework; not a local causal diagnosis.

claims.statement: A systematic integrative review identifies literacy, affordability, accessible content and infrastructure as distinct dimensions of digital inequity.
claims.boundary: Review concentrated on developed-country studies.

claims.statement: ITU DataHub provides connectivity indicators for country and regional comparison.
claims.boundary: Dataset availability is not a deployed inclusion intervention.

claims.statement: WMO's 2025 water assessment documents abnormal river flows, declining land-water storage and continuing gaps in hydrological observations.
claims.boundary: Hydrological model and station coverage differ across regions.

claims.statement: WMO HydroSOS documents an initiative for hydrological status, outlooks and national capacity building.
claims.boundary: Do not infer operational reach or forecasting accuracy in any locality.

claims.statement: IEA reports that approximately 730 million people lack electricity access, while many institutions with connections still face unreliable modern energy services.
claims.boundary: Global estimates, not local service quality measurements.

claims.statement: IEA's ACCESS scenario models possible country-specific routes toward modern electricity and clean-cooking services.
claims.boundary: Scenario is modelling, not a deployed access program or measured effectiveness.

claims.statement: WHO and the World Bank track essential health-service coverage separately from financial hardship due to out-of-pocket spending.
claims.boundary: Service coverage is observed through 2023 and hardship through 2022; revised indicators.

claims.statement: WHO provides a UHC monitoring portal with service-coverage and financial-protection indicators.
claims.boundary: Data portal does not itself deliver health services.

claims.statement: The 2025 FAO-led SOFI assessment links food-price inflation with reduced purchasing power and access to healthy diets.
claims.boundary: Aggregate associations do not determine a given household's nutritional outcomes.

claims.statement: UN-Habitat's 2026 housing report documents affordability pressures alongside informality, displacement, climate risk and adequacy concerns.
claims.boundary: Global framing; measurement and definitions differ across cities.

claims.statement: OECD's Affordable Housing Database publishes cross-national indicators of costs, housing conditions and housing policies.
claims.boundary: Primarily OECD/EU/key partners; monitoring is not proof of improved affordability.

claims.statement: The WHO/UNICEF 2025 JMP report estimates that 2.1 billion people lacked safely managed drinking water in 2024, with substantial inequality.
claims.boundary: Modelled estimates with uneven country and indicator coverage.

claims.statement: The WHO/UNICEF JMP data service publishes water, sanitation and hygiene monitoring indicators.
claims.boundary: Dataset is not an implemented water-supply service.

claims.statement: IEA's grid stocktake describes transmission and interconnection bottlenecks as potential constraints on expanding electricity supply and renewable integration.
claims.boundary: Global stocktake and scenarios; no individual grid verified.

claims.statement: A 2025 technical review surveys grid-enhancing technologies including dynamic line ratings, power-flow controls and topology optimization.
claims.boundary: Review of methods and deployment barriers; not independent proof of system-wide gains.

claims.statement: A systematic review identifies crop diversification, climate-resilient varieties and precision tools as adaptation approaches with uneven evidence on system-level and equity outcomes.
claims.boundary: Review synthesis; no specific location's intervention evaluated here.

claims.statement: UNESCO's 2026 SDG 4 monitoring separates school participation from learning proficiency; its global primary reading-proficiency estimate has not been updated since COVID-19.
claims.boundary: Learning assessment coverage and timeliness are limited.

claims.statement: World Bank Country Learning Poverty Briefs combine schooling and reading-proficiency indicators for country comparisons.
claims.boundary: Indicator depends on assessments and assumptions about out-of-school children.

claims.statement: World Bank's Global Education Policy Dashboard measures selected system drivers associated with foundational learning.
claims.boundary: Measurement of drivers is not demonstrated learning improvement.

claims.statement: A 2026 systematic review distinguishes foundation-model privacy threats, mitigation techniques and trade-offs.
claims.boundary: A review does not demonstrate an actual leak in a specific deployment.

claims.statement: Taiwan's 2024 official free-roaming-dog population estimate was 141,584; the reported change since 2022 was not statistically significant.
claims.boundary: National periodic survey; not continuous local population enumeration.

claims.statement: A systematic review surveys free-ranging dog population estimation methods and their methodological assumptions.
claims.boundary: Method review; no estimator independently executed here.

claims.statement: ICAM's Talea documentation describes street-dog sighting capture; its user guide does not support attaching animal photos to individual sightings.
claims.boundary: Documentation alone does not establish capture-recapture identification or effectiveness.

bridges.boundary: Meaningful digital service generally requires power, but a connection does not ensure use or reliable service.
General connectivity and educational connectivity overlap but are not identical; no measured learning effect established.
Digital service channels may influence access, not replace physical primary-care capacity; contextual lead only.
Hydrological observations can inform adaptation planning; no location-specific program effect demonstrated.
Groundwater is one of several WMO hydrological monitoring dimensions; observation does not control depletion.
Food affordability relates to nutrition and health risks; this is not an estimated NCD causal effect.
Housing costs and health affordability may share household-resource constraints; no causal geography-specific evidence attached.
Grid bottlenecks may affect reliability; this is not a universal explanation of electricity access gaps.
Water and health service systems share public-service constraints but require different indicators.
Energy reliability is a candidate productive-infrastructure dependency for cooling and post-harvest logistics.
Housing affordability and homelessness are related but distinct phenomena; no causal estimate attached.
